newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit dips to 2.51/dlr on official's comment.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit dips to 2.51/dlr on official's comment.

text.p: The ringgit dipped below the psychological 2.51 a dollar barrier after a Bank Negara official said in Hong Kong that the option of capital controls may be considered to control "hot money" flows, dealers said.
They said a strong dollar/yen and selling in dollar/Sing, which triggered unwinding of ringgit/Sing, also pressured the Malaysian unit downward despite mild profit-taking around 2.51 level.
At 0700 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5103/08 a dollar against 2.5068/75 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Friday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5643/48 a ringgit against 0.5649/54.

Zeti Akhtar Aziz, a Bank Negara Assistant Governor, told a conference sponsored by research firm I.D.E.A. that capital curbs was one of three options that could be considered if short-term capital flows played a dominant role in fund flows.
The others were allowing the country's currency to appreciate or increasing foreign exchange reserves.
She, however, said that Bank Negara would intervene in the foreign exchange market only if dollar/ringgit moved in divergence to the country's changing economic fundamentals.
Dealers said the comment had made the market nervous because Bank Negara has in the past imposed capital controls.
